request.spec:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now archive a sheet, and once it's archived every change to it is refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new archive test and the three that re-run existing features. After that run I only edited a code comment, so nothing needs re-running.

**How it works**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V36__sheet_archived.sql`, adds an `archived` column to the sheet, set to false by default. The sheet's data now includes `archived`.
- **Archiving:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/archive`, archives the sheet and writes `SHEET_ARCHIVED sheet=<id> by=<user>` to the audit file. It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, and it refuses a sheet that's already archived. A refusal writes nothing.
- **Blocking changes:** almost every change already starts with the same check that refuses viewers (`RefuseViewer`). I added the archived check there, so one edit covers the sheet's today, people, claims, rates, settings, roles, the paste box and quick-add. A refusal returns a 403 with the form's usual error.
- **Bulk actions:** bulk open and bulk settle don't go through that check. On an archived sheet they now open or settle nothing and report every selected claim as refused (for example `{opened: 0, refused: 1}`).
- **Screen:** the sheet header shows "Archived yes/no" (`sheet-archived`) next to an Archive button (`sheet-archive`). The today form and the button share the one `sheet-error` element, because the test can't tell two elements with the same `data-testid` apart. Using one form clears the other's error.

**Choices you may want to revisit**
- I gave the archived refusal a 403, not a 409. In the app's front end, a 409 already means "someone else changed this". The person editor, for example, re-reads the person and resets the form when it gets one.
- The archive button's error doesn't say why it was refused. It reads "Only a steward may archive the sheet, once." for both a non-steward and an already-archived sheet, because both come back as a 403.
- Archiving can't be undone. The request didn't ask for un-archiving, so I didn't add it.
